# Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta (MN 9 (PTS MN i 46))

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sammādiṭṭhi Sutta* (MN 9) is delivered by the Venerable Sāriputta to his fellow mendicants, providing a comprehensive, systematic exposition of right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*), the initial factor of the noble eightfold path [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2005]. Typical of Sāriputta's analytical teaching method, the discourse proceeds by dissecting the topic into fine components rather than employing literary embellishment [Nyanaponika, Hecker, and Bodhi 2003]. He elaborates sixteen distinct aspects of right view, treating unwholesome and wholesome action along with their respective roots, the four nutriments (*āhāra*), the four noble truths, the twelve factors of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) with analytical definitions (such as defining mentality, *nāma*, at MN 9.54), and the taints (*āsava*) as conditions for ignorance [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995; Thakchoe and Garfield 2007]. Its commentary differentiates right view into conceptual understanding conforming to the truths (*saccānulomika-sammādiṭṭhi*) and experiential wisdom directly penetrating them (*saccapaṭivedha-sammādiṭṭhi*) [Bodhi 2005; Thakchoe and Garfield 2007].
Parallels identified by SuttaCentral include discourse versions in the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 29) and *Saṁyukta Āgama* (SĀ 344), Aṅguttara Nikāya AN 9.13, a Sanskrit fragment (SF 172), and sections of the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (DN 22 and MN 10) [SuttaCentral; Anālayo 2016]. In agreement with SuttaCentral's identification of the *Saṁyukta Āgama* parallel, DharmaNexus aligns MN 9 with T 99 (SĀ 344), as well as the Tibetan *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D 4094), Sanskrit and Tibetan recensions of the *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, and the *Mahāvastu* [DharmaNexus]. Pali-internal text reuse recorded by DharmaNexus exceeds 6,100 matches across 159 texts, showing extensive shared doctrinal sequences with the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Saccakathā* (Ps 2.2), and the Vibhaṅga (*Saccavibhaṅga* and *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga*) [DharmaNexus].
